topicName: Secrets Management in CI/CD (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Secrets Management in CI/CD (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Hardcoding credentials, API keys, and database passwords in source code or CI/CD configuration files is a critical security vulnerability. As pipelines become more complex, managing secrets securely across multiple environments requires robust enterprise tools like HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager. This tutorial explores architectural patterns and implementation steps for integrating these tools into modern CI/CD workflows."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Secrets Management Architecture"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In a secure CI/CD pipeline, secrets should never reside statically in configuration files or plain text environment variables. Instead, pipelines should fetch secrets dynamically at runtime, use them strictly within the scope of execution, and revoke them immediately afterwards."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"HashiCorp Vault: An identity-based secret and encryption management system. It provides dynamic secrets, encryption-as-a-service, and tight access control using robust authentication methods like OIDC and AppRole."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"AWS Secrets Manager: A fully managed service that helps you rotate, manage, and retrieve database credentials, API keys, and other secrets throughout their lifecycle with native AWS IAM integration."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Integrating HashiCorp Vault with GitHub Actions"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"HashiCorp Vault can authenticate external CI/CD runners using OpenID Connect (OIDC). This eliminates the need to store long-lived tokens in your repository settings."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"name: Deploy with Vault Secrets
on: [push]
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate to Vault
        uses: hashicorp/vault-action@v2
        with:
          url: 'https://vault.internal.net'
          method: jwt
          role: 'ci-cd-deployment-role'
          secrets: |
            secret/data/ci/aws access_key | AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID;
            secret/data/ci/aws secret_key | AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Integrating AWS Secrets Manager with GitLab CI/CD"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"When using AWS resources, AWS Secrets Manager allows your pipelines to securely retrieve secrets using IAM roles assumed via AWS Security Token Service (STS)."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"stages:
  - deploy

deploy_job:
  stage: deploy
  image: amazon/aws-cli:latest
  script:
    - export DB_PASSWORD=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id "prod/database/password" --query "SecretString" --output text)
    - echo "Deploying application using fetched credentials..."
    - ./deploy.sh"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Secret Rotation and Auditing"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enforce Short-Lived Tokens: Configure Vault leases with minimal TTL (Time-To-Live) values so that leaked credentials expire automatically."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enable Audit Logging: Ensure comprehensive audit trails are enabled in both Vault and AWS CloudTrail to track exactly who accessed which secret and when."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mask Secrets in Logs: Configure your CI/CD platform (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins) to automatically mask environment variables containing sensitive outputs to prevent accidental exposure."}]
